guide.smokeleafindustries.power_and_pipe: $(bold)The Generator$() is the only source of FE (Forge Energy) in this mod. Feed it weed, bud, Hemp Coal, or a bucket of Hash Oil and it burns the fuel to fill its own 64,000 FE internal buffer.$(br)$(br)Once it has power, the Generator automatically pushes $(bold)40 FE per tick$() to every one of its 6 neighboring blocks that can accept energy — including an Energy Pipe placed directly against it.$(br)$(br)Every processing machine (Grinder, Extractor, Liquifier, Mixer, Mutator, Strain Identifier, Synthesizer, Sequencer, Dryer, Confectioner) has its own 64,000 FE buffer and draws $(bold)20 FE per tick$() while actively crafting. Keep at least one Generator running, or your machines will simply sit idle once their buffers run dry.
The Generator: build one early, it's the backbone of everything else.

Pipes automate moving items, fluids, and FE between machines instead of you carrying everything by hand.$(br)$(br)There are 3 separate pipe types — $(bold)Item Pipe$(), $(bold)Fluid Pipe$(), and $(bold)Energy Pipe$() — and up to $(bold)all three can occupy the same block position at once$(), each running its own independent network.$(br)$(br)A freshly placed pipe isn't connected to anything yet. Every face of a pipe segment is either $(bold)NONE$() (capped), $(bold)PIPE$() (joined to a neighboring pipe of the same type), $(bold)IMPORT$() (pulling from an adjacent machine into the network), or $(bold)EXPORT$() (pushing from the network into an adjacent machine). Use the $(bold)Pipe Wrench$() to set these — see the next page.
Item Pipe — moves items between inventories (machine slots, chests).
Fluid Pipe — moves fluids between tanks (oils, mixture fluids).
Energy Pipe — carries FE onward from a Generator to machines it isn't directly touching.

The $(bold)Pipe Wrench$() connects and disconnects pipes. What happens depends on exactly where you click:$(br)$(br)$(bold)Plain right-click$() on an empty (capped) connector grows a new connection toward the face you clicked — it becomes $(bold)PIPE$() if you're facing another pipe of the same type, or $(bold)IMPORT$() if you're facing a machine.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Plain right-click$() on an $(bold)existing$() connector: if it links to another pipe, it disconnects; if it links to a machine, it cycles $(bold)IMPORT -> EXPORT -> disconnected$().

$(bold)Shift + right-click$() anywhere on one pipe type removes that whole type from the block — it drops the pipe item, and removes the block entirely if it was the last type present.$(br)$(br)Since Item/Fluid/Energy Pipes can share one position, you can right-click the same spot with a different pipe item to add a second or third type there, then wrench each type's connections independently.
The Pipe Wrench — keep it on your hotbar whenever you're laying pipe.

Has durability just like a diamond pickaxe (and can take $(bold)Unbreaking$() and $(bold)Mending$()) — every successful wrench action costs 1 durability, but a no-op click (nothing to connect to) doesn't.

$(bold)Goal:$() feed a Grinder's ground weed straight into an Extractor without touching it by hand.$(br)$(br)1. Place an $(bold)Item Pipe$() between the Grinder's output side and the Extractor's input side.$(br)2. Right-click the pipe's connector facing the $(bold)Grinder$() with the Pipe Wrench so it's set to $(bold)EXPORT$() (right-click it again, plain, if it comes up Import first -- shift+right-click would remove the whole pipe type instead) so items leave the Grinder.$(br)3. Right-click the connector facing the $(bold)Extractor$() and set it to $(bold)IMPORT$() so the network pushes into the Extractor's input.$(br)$(br)The same pattern works for Fluid Pipes between tanks, and Energy Pipes carrying power from a Generator onward to a machine several blocks away.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.manua: A held tool that grinds bud into weed by hand — no FE required, and no machine to build first. $(bold)Craft it together with a Bud$() (any stack size, in one slot or spread across up to three) to load it with up to 3 buds, then hold it in your main hand and $(bold)hold Right Click$() to grind — one bud is consumed per grind, so loading 3 at once means you can grind three times before reloading.$(br)$(br)Once you have a real $(bold)Grinder$() block, the Manual Grinder becomes mostly a backup — the machine version is faster and doesn't take up your hand.
Crafted from Stone, Hemp Fibers, and Iron Ingot.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.grind: Grinds a bud into weed. $(bold)Dried buds give a +1 output bonus$() over fresh ones, so drying before grinding is worth the extra step.$(br)$(br)Draws 20 FE/tick while running; needs a Generator (directly adjacent or via Energy Pipe) to operate.
Needs Hemp Core — the universal machine-tier gate ingredient.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.dryin: A free, unpowered drying block with $(bold)12 independent slots$() (3 layers of 4). Each slot dries its own bud over time — slower than the powered Dryer, but costs no FE at all.$(br)$(br)Drying doesn't change a strain's effects; it just gives a bonus Weed when the dried bud is later ground (Manual Grinder or Grinder).
Just Iron Ingot, Hemp Fibers, and planks — buildable before you have any machine tier at all.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.dryer: The powered version of the Drying Rack — dries a single bud much faster using FE instead of just time.$(br)$(br)Its crafting recipe uses an already-built $(bold)Drying Rack$() as a component, so build that first.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.extra: Turns raw plant items into intermediate reagents, carrying the strain's data along with them: weed/bud -> $(bold)Extract$(), Hemp Seeds -> $(bold)DNA Strand$(), Hemp Leaf -> $(bold)Bio Composite$().$(br)$(br)Draws 20 FE/tick while running.
The first machine you'll want once your hand-tool chain is running.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.liqui: Melts a solid item into an oil fluid: weed -> 250mB Hash Oil, Hemp Leaf -> 50mB Hash Oil, or a generic Extract -> 250mB Unidentified Mixture Fluid — all still carrying the source strain's data.$(br)$(br)This is the machine that turns solid strain items into the oil "currency" used by the Mixer, Mutator, and Confectioner.
Needs a Bucket and Gold Ingot alongside the usual Hemp Core shell.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.gener: The mod's only power source — see the Power & Pipes category for how fuel, FE storage, and neighbor-pushing work.
Iron, Hemp Plastic, and a Furnace at its core.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.mixer: The strain-breeding step. Pour two $(bold)different$() strains' oils into Tank A and Tank B; the Mixer blends their colors, THC/CBD, N-P-K targets, and effect lists (amount-weighted) into one new $(bold)unidentified$() hybrid oil.$(br)$(br)See the "Making Your Own Strain" category for the full walkthrough.
Now has a proper crafting recipe — no longer creative-only.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.mutat: Takes $(bold)Hemp Seeds$() + a $(bold)Base Extract$() + the mixed oil (from a Mixer) in its tank, and crafts a brand-new seed stamped with the blended $(bold)StrainData$() — still unidentified until you run it through the Strain Identifier.
One of the two "end-game" machines, alongside the Synthesizer.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.strai: Spend $(bold)Hemp Leaf$() as currency (a "leaf meter", capped at 256) to nudge an unidentified custom strain's THC, CBD, leaf color and strain color, then give it a name.$(br)$(br)Saving deducts leaf cost based on how far you pushed the stats, marks the seed $(bold)identified$(), and registers it server-wide so every copy of that strain updates.
Now has a proper crafting recipe — no longer creative-only.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.synth: Embeds 3 specific reagent items into a DNA Strand to make a $(bold)Filled DNA Strand$() targeting one exact preset strain — each of the 25 base strains has its own reagent recipe.
Feed the Filled DNA Strand into the Sequencer next.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.seque: Takes a Filled DNA Strand plus a $(bold)Base Extract$() and outputs a guaranteed, already-identified Extract of that exact preset strain — the deterministic alternative to gambling on villager trades.
Needs a Base Extract per operation — keep a stock crafted ahead of time.
guide.smokeleafindustries.machines.gummy: Needs a reusable $(bold)mold$() (never consumed), a $(bold)catalyst$() item consumed per craft (Sugar for gummy bears, Honey Bottle for gummy worms), and 250mB of any strain oil in its tank. Produces a gummy stamped with that oil's strain.
Crafted from the same Hemp Plastic/Hemp Core frame as every other machine, with a Hopper at its core -- no longer the old all-vanilla iron/hopper/redstone recipe.
guide.smokeleafindustries.category.effec: What smoking and eating your strains actually does to you.
guide.smokeleafindustries.category.edibl: Gummies, baked goods, tinctures, and smoking devices.
guide.smokeleafindustries.category.items: Miscellaneous reference: reagents, bags, tools, and trackers.
guide.smokeleafindustries.effects.how_ef: $(bold)Eating an edible$() (a Gummy, Weed Cookie, Hash Brownie, or Herb Cake) applies that strain's own signature effect, for a duration scaled by its CBD (10 seconds at 0% CBD, up to 25 seconds at the 30% CBD cap). Raw Bud and Weed aren't edible on their own -- you have to turn them into something first.$(br)$(br)Higher $(bold)THC$() adds bonus random-but-strain-consistent extra effects on top of the signature one:$(br)- 0-10% THC: signature effect only$(br)- 10-15% THC: +1 extra effect$(br)- 15-25% THC: +2 extra effects$(br)- 25-35% THC: +3 extra effects

Using a $(bold)Bong, Blunt, Joint, or Dab Rig$() applies the exact same strain effect(s) as eating an edible made from it - $(bold)plus$() it always grants the universal $(bold)Stoned$() effect on top.$(br)$(br)Stoned's intensity is a "trip tier" driven by THC: 12 escalating tiers from Mellow Buzz up to Cosmic Couchlock, with the top 3 tiers (THC 26+) intentionally disorienting to look at. High CBD (27-30%) shortens how long Stoned lasts by up to 60%.
guide.smokeleafindustries.effects.stoned: $(bold)Stoned$() is the universal "high" effect - you get it from smoking devices (Joint, Blunt, Bong, Dab Rig) and from eating edibles (Gummies, Weed Cookie, Hash Brownie, Herb Cake), though never from raw Bud or Weed, which aren't edible at all. Its amplifier is a THC-driven $(bold)trip tier$(): the higher the THC of what you smoked or ate, the more intense (and the more visually distorted) the effect.$(br)$(br)The visuals only kick in after a few hits from the $(bold)same item$() in a row - a single puff won't do much.
The $(bold)Bong$() is the simplest way to get Stoned - smoke any strain's Weed through it (it only accepts Weed, not raw Bud).
The $(bold)Dab Rig$() consumes concentrated oil for a stronger, faster hit than the Bong.
guide.smokeleafindustries.effects.mind_a: $(bold)Sleepy$() - makes you drift and sway sideways as you walk, like you're drunk, and slows you down.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Relaxed$() - a light, calming passive effect.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Euphoric$() - forces you to sprint and slightly reduces hunger drain while it lasts.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Uplifted$() - gives your steps a spring: extra horizontal momentum and a jump-boost feel.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Chillout$() - a calming effect that also pacifies nearby zombies.
guide.smokeleafindustries.effects.sensor: $(bold)Scrambled Mouth$() - garbles what you say.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Dry Mouth$() and $(bold)Dizzy$() - mirror vanilla Nausea and Confusion onto your screen for as long as they last.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Dry Eyes$() - tints your vision with a reddened haze.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Echo Location$() - a sonar-like sense effect.
guide.smokeleafindustries.effects.social: $(bold)Aroused$() - pulls nearby animals and villagers toward you.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Shy$() - turns you invisible while sneaking.$(br)$(br)$(bold)High Flyer$() - grants Creative-style flight for as long as it lasts.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Sticky Icky$() - magnetically pulls nearby dropped items and XP orbs toward you (with a grace period so your own fresh drops aren't instantly re-sucked).$(br)$(br)$(bold)Friend or Foe$() and $(bold)Linguists High$() - situational strain-flavored effects.
guide.smokeleafindustries.effects.hazard: $(bold)Paranoia$() - randomly spawns fake spooky sounds and hallucinated mobs that aren't really there.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Brain Melt$() - a disorienting harmful effect.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Zombified$() - if you're standing in direct sunlight without a helmet, you'll catch fire (or your helmet takes the damage instead) just like a zombie or husk.
guide.smokeleafindustries.effects.strain: A few effects are tied to a specific preset strain's signature: $(bold)R Trees$() (Jack Herer) and $(bold)Vein High$() (Carbon Fiber) are two examples - check a strain's own Guide page or its Strain Data Pad entry to see exactly which signature effect it grants.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Rainbow, Breathing, Bubbled,$() and $(bold)Melted$() round out the rest of the signature pool - mostly visual/atmospheric effects flavoring a particular strain's high.
guide.smokeleafindustries.edibles_and_co: The Confectioner (Gummy Machine)
Making Gummies

The $(bold)Confectioner$() (internally called the "Gummy Machine") turns any strain's oil into a strain-stamped gummy. It needs three things at once:$(br)- A $(bold)mold$() in its mold slot - never consumed, reusable forever$(br)- A $(bold)catalyst$() - consumed every craft$(br)- 250mB of $(bold)any oil fluid$() in its tank$(br)$(br)The output gummy inherits whichever strain's oil you fed it, effects and all.
The $(bold)Gummy Bear Mold$() uses $(bold)Sugar$() as its catalyst.
The $(bold)Gummy Worm Mold$() uses a $(bold)Honey Bottle$() as its catalyst instead, and gives a slightly shorter effect duration than a gummy bear.
Crafting the Confectioner block itself:
Baked Edibles
Weed Cookie, Hash Brownie, Herb Cake

These three are plain $(bold)crafting-table$() recipes, not machine outputs - include a strain's Weed as one of the ingredients and the result copies that strain's effects onto the finished edible automatically.
$(bold)Weed Cookie$() - a quick, simple infused snack.
$(bold)Hash Brownie$() - a heavier baked edible.
$(bold)Herb Cake$() - the biggest of the three, built from $(bold)Infused Butter$() plus a strain ingredient.
Tinctures
Tinctures

A $(bold)Tincture$() is a bottled, strain-infused liquid consumable - fill an $(bold)Empty Vial$() with Hash Oil to make a $(bold)Hash Oil Tincture$(). A discreet, quick way to get a strain's effects without smoking or eating a full edible.
Start from an Empty Tincture before filling it with oil.
Smoking Devices
How You Actually Smoke

$(bold)Bong, Blunt, Joint,$() and $(bold)Dab Rig$() are the four ways to smoke a strain. All four apply the strain's own effects $(bold)plus$() the universal $(bold)Stoned$() effect - see the Effects tab for exactly how Stoned's intensity and duration work.
The $(bold)Blunt$() and $(bold)Joint$() are rolled, portable smokes.
The $(bold)Dab Rig$() hits concentrated oil for a stronger effect.
guide.smokeleafindustries.items.dna_stra: A $(bold)DNA Strand$() is a reusable carrier item: embed 3 specific reagent items into it (each preset strain has its own reagent recipe - check that strain's own Guide entry), then feed the filled strand into the $(bold)Synthesizer$() to move toward that strain's extract.

This has to happen in the $(bold)Synthesizer$() - drop the empty DNA Strand and 3 reagent items into it together. The exact 3 items you use matter: they're checked later in the $(bold)Sequencer$() to decide which strain you get. Shown here is White Widow's own combo (Cobweb, Snowball, White Dye) as an example - other strains need completely different reagents.
guide.smokeleafindustries.items.base_ext: $(bold)Base Extract$() is a plain crafting-table reagent required by the $(bold)Sequencer$() - one is consumed per sequencing operation. Keep a stack ready before you start sequencing strain extracts.
guide.smokeleafindustries.items.bags.pag: A $(bold)Bag$() compacts a strain's Weed into denser, easier-to-carry storage - mainly useful for selling to villagers or long-distance hauling. Start from an $(bold)Empty Bag$() and fill it with a strain's weed.
guide.smokeleafindustries.items.strain_d: Right-click the $(bold)Strain Data Pad$() (a.k.a. the Strain Book) to open a two-tab viewer: $(bold)Personal$() lists every strain you've personally discovered, and $(bold)Server$() lists every strain anyone on the server has ever registered, crediting its original discoverer. See the Making Your Own Strain tab for the full strain-creation walkthrough this pad tracks.
guide.smokeleafindustries.items.early_to: Three hand tools carry you through the earliest part of the game, before any machine exists:
The $(bold)Hemp Hammer$() smashes Hemp Leaves into Bio Composite - the first step toward Hemp Plastic and the Hemp Core every machine needs.

The $(bold)Manual Grinder$() grinds bud into weed by hand, before you've built a Grinder machine: craft it together with a Bud to load it, then hold it in your main hand and hold Right Click to grind.
The $(bold)Plant Analyzer$() lets you inspect a crop's live stats (THC/CBD/N-P-K) without harvesting it.
guide.smokeleafindustries.items.hemp_woo: $(bold)Hemp Wool$() is a woven building block made from Hemp Fabric — its weave and faint green-yellow tint set it apart from ordinary sheep's wool. It comes in all 16 dye colors: craft the plain block from Hemp Fabric, then dye it just like vanilla wool by combining any Hemp Wool with a dye of the color you want.
guide.smokeleafindustries.items.baja_hoo: A hooded set of armor woven from $(bold)Hemp Fabric$(), protecting about as well as leather armor. Wear the full set — helmet, chestplate, leggings, and boots — and it $(bold)negates the Stoned effect$() entirely, letting you smoke or eat an edible without getting high. Like any vanilla armor, it can be enchanted and trimmed at the smithing table.
Crafting the chestplate (the other 3 pieces use Hemp Fabric in the usual vanilla armor shapes):

Upgrade each piece at a crafting table with $(bold)1 Hemp Plastic + 1 Netherite Ingot$() to get the $(bold)Reinforced Baja Hoodie$() — netherite-tier armor with $(bold)1 more protection per piece$() than plain netherite armor, while still negating the Stoned effect in a full set. The upgrade keeps whatever enchantments and trims the base piece already had.
guide.smokeleafindustries.category.getti: From breaking your first tall grass to your first identified strain.
guide.smokeleafindustries.category.growi: Field crops, Grow Pots, and how light and lamps speed growth.
guide.smokeleafindustries.category.nutri: How Nitrogen, Phosphorus and Potassium control your yield and potency.
guide.smokeleafindustries.getting_starte: Welcome, Grower

$(bold)Smokeleaf Industries$() turns growing and processing plants into a full tech tree: grow crops, dry and grind them, extract oils, blend your own strains, and automate everything with power and pipes.$(br)$(br)This category walks you step by step from nothing to your first real strain. Work through it in order using the $(bold)forward arrow$() at the bottom of the page. Other tabs on the left cover Growing, Nutrients, Power & Pipes, Machines, Strains, Making Your Own Strain, Effects, Edibles, and general Items in more depth once you're up and running.
Your First Seeds

Break $(bold)tall grass$() in the overworld — it has a chance to drop $(bold)Hemp Seeds$(). Hemp is the mod's starter crop: it grows about 3.5x faster than every other strain, so it's the best way to get your economy moving before you have any machines at all.
Hemp Seeds. Plant these on farmland to begin.
Planting

Till dirt or grass into $(bold)farmland$() with a hoe, ideally within a few blocks of water so it stays hydrated. Right click the farmland with Hemp Seeds to plant.$(br)$(br)Like vanilla crops, your plant needs a light level of $(bold)11 or higher$() to grow — plant outdoors or under a light source. No fertilizer is required to grow hemp, but it does grow faster with fertilizer or Bone Meal.
Harvesting Hemp

Hemp grows through $(bold)11 age stages (0-10)$() and becomes a full two-block-tall plant once mature.$(br)$(br)Once grown, you can $(bold)shear$() the plant up to 3 times to collect a Hemp Leaf each time without destroying it — the 4th interaction fully harvests it. A full harvest drops Hemp Leaf, Hemp Seeds, and Hemp Fibers.$(br)$(br)Plant many hemp crops early — you'll need a large supply of all three drops for tools and the machine tier.
Hemp Leaf — turns into Bio Composite (with a Hemp Hammer) or DNA-chain reagents.
Hemp Fibers — used by the Hemp Hammer, Manual Grinder, and Drying Rack.
First Tools

Before you have any powered machines, two hand tools let you start processing plants:$(br)$(br)$(bold)Manual Grinder$() — craft it together with a Bud to load it, then hold it in your main hand and hold Right Click to grind it into Weed, no power needed.$(br)$(bold)Hemp Hammer$() — used to smash Hemp Leaves into Bio Composite, the first step toward the machine tier.
The Manual Grinder: a slow but free alternative to the Grinder machine.
The Hemp Hammer: your gateway to Bio Composite.
The Hemp Core Chain

Every powered machine in this mod needs a $(bold)Hemp Core$() somewhere in its recipe — it's the universal tech gate. The chain to get one:$(br)$(br)Hemp Leaves + Hemp Hammer $(bold)->$() Bio Composite $(bold)->$() (smelt) Hemp Plastic$(br)Bio Composite + Diamond $(bold)->$() Unfinished Hemp Core$(br)Unfinished Hemp Core + Hemp Plastic + Hemp Hammer $(bold)->$() Hemp Core
Bio Composite: hammer 3 Hemp Leaves and 1 Hemp Fibers together.
Smelt Bio Composite into Hemp Plastic.
Hemp Core: the key ingredient every machine below needs.
Your First Machines

With Hemp Core in hand, build in roughly this order:$(br)$(br)$(bold)Generator$() — your only source of power, burns Weed, Bud, Hemp Coal, or Hash Oil.$(br)$(bold)Drying Rack$() — free, slow, dries buds without power.$(br)$(bold)Grinder$() — the powered upgrade over the Manual Grinder.$(br)$(bold)Extractor$() — turns Weed into Extract, your first step toward oils.$(br)$(br)See the Machines tab for full details on every machine, and Power & Pipes for wiring them together.
The Generator: place fuel in it and it fills its own energy buffer, then pushes power to adjacent machines.
Getting Your First Strain

The mod ships 25 preset strains (see the Strains tab). There are two ways to get one identified and ready to plant:$(br)$(br)$(bold)Buy one$() — the Stoner and Dealer villagers occasionally sell already-identified Weed for emeralds. Pure luck, but the fastest early option.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Craft one (guaranteed)$() — fill a DNA Strand with a specific strain's 3 reagent items in the Synthesizer, then feed it plus a Base Extract into the Sequencer to get that exact strain's Extract. Check a strain's page on the Strains tab for its reagent trio.
DNA Strand — fill it with a strain's 3 reagents in the Synthesizer.
Base Extract — a crafted reagent the Sequencer consumes every time it runs.
White Widow — one of the 25 starting strains, shown here as a Bud.
What's Next?

You now have a strain, basic tools, and your first machines. From here:$(br)$(br)• $(bold)Nutrients$() — learn how N-P-K controls your THC/CBD and bud count.$(br)• $(bold)Power & Pipes$() — automate transport between machines instead of doing it by hand.$(br)• $(bold)Machines$() — every machine's full inputs and outputs.$(br)• $(bold)Making Your Own Strain$() — cross two strains into something new.$(br)• $(bold)Effects & Edibles$() — what all of this is actually for.
guide.smokeleafindustries.growing_plants: Named strains (the 25 presets) grow as standard two-block-tall field crops, just like Hemp. They need a light level of $(bold)11 or higher$() to progress and farmland (or compatible soil) to be planted on.$(br)$(br)Harvesting a mature plant drops seeds plus one or more Bud, with the exact bud count and potency driven by how well you've matched its Nitrogen/Phosphorus/Potassium — see the Nutrients tab.

The Grow Pot is a self-contained planter: put a soil item inside, then a seed. It needs a light level of $(bold)12 or higher$() directly above it.$(br)$(br)Soil choice matters — $(bold)farmland-type soil$() grows a crop in about 60 seconds, other soils take about 90 seconds.$(br)$(br)Once mature, a Grow Pot will automatically try to push its harvest into an inventory placed directly below it, about once per second — handy for hooking straight into an Item Pipe or hopper for a fully automated grow room.
Craft a Grow Pot from Hemp Plastic, a Hemp Core, and a Water Bucket.

The Reflector is an empty light fixture until you insert an $(bold)HPS Bulb$() or $(bold)Dual Arc Bulb$() item into it. Once lit, it accelerates growth of crops in a small column beneath it — it does not provide the minimum light level required to grow on its own, only a growth-speed boost.$(br)$(br)Lamps have finite durability that ticks down every tick while installed, and will eventually burn out and need replacing.
Craft the empty Reflector fixture first.
HPS Bulb — a lamp item to insert into the Reflector.
Dual Arc Bulb — a longer-lasting lamp alternative.

The Grow Light is a standalone toggleable light block — right click to switch it on or off. Like the Reflector, it accelerates growth of crops in a small column beneath it, and needs no lamp item or durability management.
Craft the Grow Light from basic materials — no Hemp Core required.
guide.smokeleafindustries.nutrients.npk_: Every crop secretly tracks live $(bold)Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium$() values (0-100 each) against a target the strain wants. You raise these by right-clicking fertilizer items onto a crop that hasn't finished growing yet — once it's fully grown, fertilizing does nothing but tell you it's too late.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Match the target exactly$() and your THC/CBD is doubled and you get 3 buds instead of 1.$(br)$(bold)Get close (within a small tolerance)$() and you get 2 buds, with THC/CBD only slightly reduced.$(br)$(bold)Miss badly$() and you get only 1 bud, with potency reduced further the more you're off by.

Each of the 25 preset strains starts at its own base N-P-K and has a pre-set difficulty: Easy strains need only 1-2 fertilizer applications to max out, Medium need 2-3, Hard need 3-4, and Expert strains need 5. Custom strains you breed yourself (see Making Your Own Strain) always start at 0-0-0 and must be fertilized up from scratch to whatever target the Strain Identifier gave them.

guide.smokeleafindustries.strains.white_: $(bold)Base THC:$() 15%$(br)$(bold)Base CBD:$() 10%$(br)$(bold)Signature Effect:$() Wind Charged$(br)$(br)Higher THC unlocks extra random (but deterministic) effects on top of Wind Charged when you smoke it or eat something made from it -- see the "Reading a Strain's Stats" page for the exact thresholds.$(br)$(br)$(bold)How to get it:$() buy already-identified Weed from the Stoner or Dealer villager (luck-based), or craft it deterministically: fill a DNA Strand in the Synthesizer, then feed it plus a Base Extract and these 3 reagents into the Sequencer -- $(bold)Cobweb, Snowball, White Dye$() -- to sequence a guaranteed White Widow Extract.
White Widow bud -- eat it raw for its effects, or dry and grind it first for a stronger dose.

guide.smokeleafindustries.strains._stats: Every strain has a base $(bold)THC$() (0-35%) and $(bold)CBD$() (0-30%) percentage that decides what happens when you consume it.$(br)$(br)$(bold)THC controls how many effects you get:$()$(br)0-10% THC = just the strain's own signature effect$(br)10-15% THC = +1 extra effect$(br)15-25% THC = +2 extra effects$(br)25-35% THC = +3 extra effects$(br)Extra effects are picked from a shared pool, but always the $(bold)same$() ones for a given strain -- it's random-looking, not actually random.$(br)$(br)$(bold)CBD controls how long the effects last:$() duration scales from about 10 seconds at 0% CBD up to 25 seconds at the 30% CBD cap.

You can't eat raw Bud or Weed directly -- they aren't food. Turn a strain into something consumable first:$(br)$(br)$(bold)Smoke it$() (Joint, Blunt, Bong, or Dab Rig) -- applies the strain's effects $(bold)plus$() the universal $(bold)Stoned$() effect, whose intensity ("trip tier") is driven by THC -- see the Effects tab for details. The higher a strain's THC, the more intense (and disorienting) smoking it gets.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Eat something made from it$() -- a Gummy (from the Confectioner), or a baked edible (Weed Cookie, Hash Brownie, Herb Cake) -- applies the strain's effects for a CBD-scaled duration, and has its own separate chance to also grant Stoned.$(br)$(br)See the Machines tab for how to identify an unidentified seed, and the Making Your Own Strain tab if you'd rather breed something that isn't one of the 25 presets covered in this tab.
guide.smokeleafindustries.making_your_ow: Want a strain that isn't one of the 25 presets? You can breed your own from any two strains you already have. The full chain is:$(br)$(br)1. $(bold)Extractor$() -- bud/weed -> Extract$(br)2. $(bold)Liquifier$() -- Extract -> an oil fluid$(br)3. $(bold)Mixer$() -- two different strains' oils -> one blended (unidentified) oil$(br)4. $(bold)Mutator$() -- Hemp Seeds + Base Extract + blended oil -> an unidentified custom seed$(br)5. $(bold)Strain Identifier$() -- spend Hemp Leaf to finalize its stats and name it$(br)6. $(bold)Strain Data Pad$() -- track everything you (and the server) have discovered$(br)$(br)The next few pages walk through each step.

The $(bold)Extractor$() turns a strain's bud or weed into an $(bold)Extract$() item, carrying that exact strain's data (THC, CBD, colors, N-P-K target).$(br)$(br)The $(bold)Liquifier$() then melts an Extract into an oil fluid in its internal tank -- this oil is the strain's data in liquid form, and it's what the Mixer and Confectioner both consume.$(br)$(br)Do this once for each of the two strains you want to cross.
The Extractor's own crafting recipe, for reference.

Pour your two different strains' oils into the $(bold)Mixer$()'s Tank A and Tank B. It blends them into a single new oil: colors, THC, CBD and N-P-K all become weighted averages of the two parents (weighted by how much of each you used), and their effect lists are combined. The result is still unidentified.$(br)$(br)Feed $(bold)Hemp Seeds$(), a $(bold)Base Extract$(), and the blended oil into the $(bold)Mutator$() to grow a brand-new, $(bold)unidentified$() custom-strain seed. Every seed produced from the same batch shares one lineage, so renaming it later updates every copy you (and anyone else) are holding.

An unidentified seed is a blank slate. Put it in the $(bold)Strain Identifier$() and feed it Hemp Leaf -- this fills a capped "leaf meter" you spend to preview and adjust THC (0-35), CBD (0-30), and the leaf/bud colors, and to type a name. The higher you push THC/CBD, the more it costs.$(br)$(br)Saving deducts the leaf cost, finalizes ("identifies") the strain, and works out its N-P-K growing target from the final THC/CBD -- higher THC demands a harder target, higher CBD makes it easier. This also registers the strain server-wide under your name.$(br)$(br)Right-click the $(bold)Strain Book$() (the Strain Data Pad) any time to see every strain you've personally discovered plus everything registered on the server, credited to whoever first identified it.
